text:
Maya (AE): Heads up — enterprise POC keeps getting a 413 when sending full conversation + attachments (they inline small images as base64). Body reported ~135KB. Using POST /v1/generate model=rw-ltr-8k. They want single-request for demo. Any quick workarounds?
Julian (SE): Can you share the raw error/gateway log?
Maya (AE): This is what they pasted from client logs:
ingest-bot: gateway: client 10.14.2.7 request rejected: request_entity_too_large, length=135024, client_max_body_size=104857
Rina (SRE): That looks like the nginx front proxy limit (about 100KB). Hosted front door currently enforces that for safety. Request never reaches the runtime.
Noah (Dev): Short-term options: 1) gzip the JSON body and set Content-Encoding: gzip (we accept compressed bodies) 2) send recent N turns + a one-line summary of older context 3) upload conversation blobs to object storage (presigned) and pass a short reference 4) chunk + reassemble using session_id and a small assemble call.
Julian (SE): Customer insists on single-call. Can we make an exception for this account?
Rina (SRE): We can't change per-account proxy limits on hosted without an infra change. We can: - offer a short-lived Dedicated sandbox where proxy limits can be relaxed - provide engineering time to add a chunked-append endpoint (longer) - recommend gzip/presign as product-approved workarounds
Maya (AE): They asked whether a larger-context model (32k) would bypass this.
Noah (Dev): Model window is about token context, not raw HTTP payload size. Switching to a 32k-window model helps only after the payload is accepted by the gateway. The HTTP body limit still applies.
Julian (SE): Practical playbook for POC handoff: 1) Ask prospect to try gzip first (fast) 2) If that fails, use presigned upload flow + pointer 3) Offer a dedicated sandbox if they need single-call for demos (ops + pricing coordination)
Rina (SRE): I'll repro with a 135KB payload and confirm exact rejection behavior and whether CDN edges also block earlier. I'll file an infra ticket.
ingest-bot: ticket INF-934 created: investigate hosted client_max_body_size 413s and add alert for sustained spike
Julian (SE): Can you draft the gzip example and a presigned flow I can paste to the customer?
Noah (Dev): Gzip example to try:
```
echo -n '{\"model\":\"rw-ltr-8k\",\"input\":\"<LONG_CHAT_WITH_BASE64>\"}' | gzip -c | \\n  curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \\\n    -H 'Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>' \\\n    -H 'Content-Encoding: gzip' \\\n    -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \\\n    --data-binary @-
```
Noah (Dev): Presigned flow sketch we use in POC docs: 1) POST /v1/uploads/initiate -> returns presigned PUT URL and an upload_id 2) Client PUTs file to presigned URL (S3) 3) POST /v1/generate {\"model\":\"..\",\"context_url\":\"s3://bucket/key\",\"upload_id\":\"...\"} 4) Backend pulls file server-side before tokenization
Julian (SE): Also note: prefer not to inline large attachments as base64 in JSON; it inflates size ~33%. Use presigned upload instead.
Maya (AE): I'll send gzip + presigned options. If they request a single-call sandbox, I'll start pricing conversation.
Rina (SRE): Pricing ops: short Dedicated evals can be offered via promo credits for two-week trials; coordinate with finance for billing code.
Julian (SE): FYI I'll add this to the sales FAQ: "If total request payload >80KB, recommend gzip or presigned uploads."
Maya (AE): Prospect tried gzip and reported success — 200 returned and tokens parsed normally. They're validating semantic fidelity now.
Rina (SRE): Good. I'll update the POC runbook and add a short blurb explaining HTTP limits vs model context windows.
Maya (AE): Thanks everyone :sparkles:
